claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' followed by the indented sub-entry 'VALUE clause, VI-49'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' then '  VALUE clause, VI-49'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items). Entries and references match the PDF; informative content.

verdict.reasoning: page-969.md holds the index one entry per line with sub-entries indented two spaces (e.g. 'Linkage Section, IV-33, X-13' then '  VALUE clause, VI-49'), which keeps the printed page's lines and hierarchy in the source text. The claim itself says every entry and page reference matches the PDF. The only issue it raises is how a Markdown renderer would reflow bare lines, and that is formatting. It is not a content discrepancy with the PDF. The rest of the page is an informative index, so no meaning changes.
